root_cause.text: The `ocfs2_group_add()` function called `ocfs2_set_new_buffer_uptodate()` with a user-controlled group buffer before validating the input and used the wrong metadata cache (`INODE_CACHE(inode)` instead of `INODE_CACHE(main_bm_inode)`), causing a BUG_ON assertion failure if the block was already cached.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "ocfs2_group_add() calls ocfs2_set_new_buffer_uptodate() on a user-controlled group block before ocfs2_verify_group_and_input() validates that block number. That helper is only valid for newly allocated metadata and asserts that the block is not already present in the chosen metadata cache." The patch moves the call after validation and switches to `INODE_CACHE(main_bm_inode)`.

Author: Joel Becker <joel.becker@oracle.com>
Date:   Tue Feb 10 20:00:41 2009 -0800

    ocfs2: Take the inode out of the metadata read/write paths.
    
    We are really passing the inode into the ocfs2_read/write_blocks()

    directly into the metadata block functions, divorcing them from the

bic_trace_step.reason: In the `ocfs2_group_add` function (fs/ocfs2/resize.c), the code calls `ocfs2_set_new_buffer_uptodate(inode, group_bh);` with `inode` instead of the correct `main_bm_inode`.
